response.passage: Welcome to the National Numismatic Museum, located in the heart of Delhi. We house over 5,000 rare coins from various dynasties. Our curator, Mr. Vikram Seth, often explains that the museum was established in 1982 to preserve India's rich economic history. Visitors often ask why the gold coins are kept in vacuum-sealed glass cases. This is because oxygen reacts with gold over time, causing the metal to lose its natural shine. Please note that our 'Gold Gallery' is closed on Mondays for maintenance. If you are visiting with a group of more than 10 people, please book your tickets in advance. We also have a special collection of copper coins from the reign of Raja Bhoj, which are displayed in the East Wing. Many students confuse our 'Gold Gallery' with the 'Old Gallery', but they are entirely different sections. Remember, our museum is a place for quiet observation, not a playground for running. We look forward to your visit!
response.summary: The National Numismatic Museum in Delhi preserves thousands of historical coins. It uses special storage to protect gold coins from damage and requires group bookings for large parties.
